summary.root_cause_counts: NONE (clean pass): 16 — h01,h02,h03,h04,h05,h06,h07,h08,h09,h11,h14,h15,h16,h17,h18,h20 | NO_COMPANY_PARAM + SILENT_PARAM_DISCARD: 1 (h12) | LIVE_DATA_DRIFT / NO_SNAPSHOT: 2 (h10, h13 — h13 compounded by CLIENT_SIDE_PAGINATION_RISK) | NO_MOVEMENT_JOURNAL_ACCESS + NO_STOCK_VALUATION_FIELD: 1 (h19). Zero hallucinations and zero WRONG answers across 20 hard questions — every failure is a disclosed capability limit or sub-tolerance drift, never an invented number. All four empty-set / non-existent / unanswerable probes (h06, h07, h08, h09) passed cleanly, and the model volunteered limitation_hit on exactly the three questions it could not fully serve (h09, h12, h19).
new_defects_found: SILENT_PARAM_DISCARD — sap_query accepts an unrecognised `company`/`companyDB` argument, returns HTTP 200 and serves Oil data anyway. Only a cross-company question (h12) exposes it; a single-company tier never can. This is more dangerous than a missing feature: a less careful model would have published Oil's ₹105.74 Cr as the ₹166.91 Cr group figure with full confidence.
NO_COMPANY_PARAM — the backend is pinned to JIVO_OIL_HANADB although the underlying sapb1 CLI supports --company. Two of three company books (₹61.2 Cr of Q1 turnover) are unreachable through the MCP.

NO_MOVEMENT_JOURNAL_ACCESS — OINM is not exposed by any tool (sap_entities searches for 'inventor'/'stock' return nothing equivalent). Movement had to be reconstructed from Invoices + DeliveryNotes + InventoryGenExits, which structurally omits warehouse transfers and produced 612 instead of 431 items (h19).

NO_STOCK_VALUATION_FIELD — Items.AvgStdPrice and MovingAveragePrice are 0 for every item company-wide; only ItemWarehouseInfoCollection.StandardAveragePrice is readable, and only for FIFO/moving-average items, so all batch-valued (bis_SNB) finished goods and raw material value at ₹0. OITW.StockValue is unreachable, making the entire ₹21.78 Cr answer underivable (h19).

NO_JOURNAL_ENTRY_BP_FILTER — JournalEntries is readable but cannot be filtered by business-partner line (JournalEntryLines/any(...) and JournalEntryLines/ShortName both rejected), so GL causation for a reconciliation gap can only be inferred by subtraction, never proven (h03's ₹19,58,688 leg).

NO_SELF_JOIN / NO_SNAPSHOT-CONSISTENT READ — duplicate detection (h17) is only possible by hauling the full 2,371-document population client-side, and multi-hundred-call answers straddle live postings with no as-of or query-timestamp guarantee. This produced two sub-tolerance mismatches against the key (h10's single ₹23 lakh SAI TRADING balance move, h13's one extra ₹18.13 lakh invoice) that could not be distinguished from client-side pagination faults.

PAGE_CAP AT SCALE — the 20-row hard cap with no exposed $skip forced ~800 calls for h16, ~1,100 for h19 and 603 for h14. At the 30-question tier this was a cost problem; at this tier it becomes a correctness problem, because hand-rolled DocEntry-cursor paging has no exactly-once guarantee (h13).
DEAD ALTERNATE BACKENDS — ecom_/oms_ tools fail with 'companion CLI binary not found', removing the only fallback route when the SAP path is company-pinned (h12).
prioritised_fixes: 1. Add a `company` enum parameter to sap_query / sap_doctor / sap_fields (JIVO_OIL_HANADB | JIVO_MART_HANADB | JIVO_BEVERAGES_HANADB), pass it through to `sapb1 --company` with a per-company re-login, and have sap_doctor enumerate reachable companies. Repairs h12 outright and unlocks the entire Mart + Beverages book (~₹61 Cr of Q1 turnover) that is currently invisible.

2. Make unknown parameters a hard error instead of a silent discard. Zero questions repaired directly, but this is the highest-severity safety fix in the run: it converts h12's near-miss (Oil reported as group) from a silent wrong answer into a loud failure. Ship it with fix 1, not after.

3. Add real server-side pagination — `skip`/`cursor` + `page_size` up to 200–1000, plus an `all: true` mode with a returned row-count checksum guaranteeing exactly-once delivery. Repairs h13 and removes the truncation/duplication risk currently latent in h02, h04, h14, h15, h16, h19 and h20 (seven questions de-risked).

4. Add server-side aggregation: `aggregate: sum|count|avg`, `group_by`, over any entity and any numeric field (incl. DocTotal−VatSum and DocTotal−PaidToDate expressions). Collapses h04, h12, h13, h14, h15, h16 and h20 from hundreds of calls to one each, and is the precondition for these questions being answerable within a normal context budget.

5. Expose the inventory layer: OINM (ItemCode, DocDate, InQty, OutQty, TransType) and OITW (OnHand, StockValue per warehouse), and document that OITM.AvgPrice is identically 0 in this database. Repairs the whole of h19 — currently the only question where the correct figure is not derivable through the server at all.

6. Allow JournalEntries to be filtered by business partner (JDT1.ShortName), or add a `sap_ledger` tool returning a party's GL lines grouped by TransType. Upgrades h03 from a correct inference to a proof and makes every future ledger-vs-open-item reconciliation self-closing.
7. Return a server query timestamp on every response and offer an as-of / consistent-snapshot mode. Eliminates the drift noise behind h10 and h13 and makes multi-call answers internally consistent.
8. Repair or remove the broken ecom_/oms_ backends ('companion CLI binary not found') so a second route exists when the SAP path is constrained.
